subject: Operator license swap & platform fee allocation — proposal
messages:
From: Owen Blake <owen@horizonhealth.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment packaging inquiry — operator license swap idea

Hey Mateo,

Thanks for taking this. We're deep into scoping a VPC deployment for several clinical sites and have a packaging question that could materially change the commercial construct. Quick summary:

- Current ask: Horizon runs 30 operator licenses across multiple sites (GPU-operator model). We're exploring swapping those into a site-anchored node entitlement and asking Redwood to offset a portion of the first-year platform fee in exchange for the license swap and a 24‑month commit.
- Our target: a 40% platform fee offset in year one (to help finance migration), then normal amortization in year two. We want to understand whether Redwood can:
  1) Accept an operator->site license conversion at list without extra per-node uplift, and
  2) Provide a migration credit (or offset) against platform fee that won't break your amortization/recognition rules.

Also: we need clarity on support tiers — we expect an SRE retainer (24/7 on-call) for initial 3 months plus standard enterprise SLA after cutover. Can you advise cost for SRE retainer vs. ad-hoc incident support?

Attached: Horizon_MAO_pricing_sheet.xlsx (current usage slices and daily token profile).

Can we get a short proposal by Friday? We're lining up procurement review the following week.

Appreciate it,
Owen
Director of Cloud Ops
Horizon Health

---


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Owen Blake <owen@horizonhealth.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment packaging inquiry — operator license swap idea

Owen — thanks for the clear brief and the spreadsheet. We can put together two packaging tracks quickly: a) Amortized platform fee with operator->site conversion (credits applied to year one) and b) Node-anchored entitlement where a portion of the platform fee is swapped for committed node credits.

Prelim notes (need to validate with finance & legal):
- Operator->site swap: feasible, we typically treat this as a SKU reclassification. We can allow conversion at list if there is a firm 24‑month commit, but the platform-fee offset will be conservative by default (we'll provide a proposal where offset ranges 20–40%).
- Migration credit: we can mix a percentage offset of platform fee and a one-time implementation credit (capable of being amortized across invoice schedule).
- SRE retainer: two flavors — Priority Retainer (24/7, two FTE SRE coverage for initial window) at $45,000/mo or Scoped War Room (time-boxed, incident-led) at $18,000/mo. The retainer includes runbook handoff and a 30‑day hypercare.

Can you confirm: a) whether Horizon prefers CAPEX (one-time invoice) or OPEX (monthly), and b) which SLA band you're targeting post-cutover (P1 response within 30 minutes vs. 1 hour)?

I'll draft a short comparison PDF and loop in pricing ops. Expect a first-pass by Wednesday EOD.

Thanks — Mateo
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: packaging-options-summary.pdf

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment packaging inquiry — need a pricing construct for Horizon (deal HZN-2026-4472)

Irene / Marissa — forwarding Horizon's ask. Key points: 30 operator licenses, asking for up to 40% platform fee offset in year one if we permit operator->site conversion with 24‑month commit. They are also asking for a 3‑month SRE retainer.

My proposed commercial constructs to present (first-pass):
1) Conservative swap (Recommended): 25% platform fee offset in year one + one-time migration credit $60k. Operator->site conversion at list; 24‑month committed consumption (minimum floor). Offer: SRE Priority Retainer at $35k/mo (discounted from standard).
2) Aggressive concession: 40% platform fee offset year one + $95k migration credit; lower retainer price $25k/mo; requires exec approval and a firm 36‑month commit.
3) Node-anchored alternative: keep operator licences, sell additional node‑entitlements; apply 30% platform fee amortization credit against first 6 months; no one-time credit.

Commercial notes:
- Finance will push back on >30% offsets without longer duration or clear revenue recognition path.
- Legal needs to sign a short amendment for SKU reclassification and a one-time credit clause.
- We should protect Redwood with fallback language that restores full platform fee if Horizon reduces usage by >30% within 12 months.

Can you run numbers (expected ARR impact, revenue recognition timing) and confirm whether we can offer the recommended Conservative swap today. If yes, I will prepare the customer-facing proposal and request approval from Sales Leadership.

Thanks — Mateo

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment packaging inquiry — need a pricing construct for Horizon (deal HZN-2026-4472)

Team — reviewed Mateo's constructs with finance. High-level guidance:
- Approve the Conservative swap as the standard outbound offer. Numbers we can support: 20% platform fee offset in year one + a one-time migration credit capped at $75,000. Offer the Priority Retainer at $35k/mo for the first 3 months, revert to $45k/mo thereafter if they want ongoing 24/7 coverage.
- If Sales wants to push to 40% offset, we need a commercial exception approved by VP Sales + Finance signoff and a minimum 36‑month contractual commitment with accelerated payment terms.
- Add a usage-protection clause: if average token consumption falls below 70% of baseline in months 4–12, the offset is clawed back proportionally.

Please proceed with the customer proposal using the Conservative swap numbers. I'll coordinate legal for the amendment and loop in Finance for the credit mechanics.

Irene
Head of Pricing & Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Owen Blake <owen@horizonhealth.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: operator->site conversion with migration credit (HZN-2026-4472)

Owen — thanks for patience. Attached is our formal proposal and a short commercial summary. Highlights below:

- Offer: Operator->site license conversion for 30 operator licenses, effective at execution.
- Commercial construct (Conservative swap — approved): 20% platform fee offset applied to invoices across first 12 months + one-time migration credit of $75,000 applied on first invoice after cutover.
- Commit: 24‑month contractual commitment to baseline consumption (minimum floor as per attached SOW).
- Support: Priority Retainer for the initial 3 months at $35,000/mo (includes 2 FTE SRE coverage, runbook handover, 30‑day hypercare). After 3 months, standard enterprise SLA applies; ongoing 24/7 retainer available at $45,000/mo.
- Safeguards: Usage-protection clause — if monthly average consumption falls below 70% of baseline in months 4–12, the offset will be clawed back proportionally. Amendment language is attached.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached redwood_privdeploy_term_sheet_v2.pdf and sign the DocuSign link (https://docusign.com/tx/ABCD-1234-sign) to accept the amendment.
2) Provide preferred billing model (CAPEX one-time credit application vs. monthly OPEX offset).
3) Confirm start date for SRE retainer window.

I've copied Irene and Marissa for visibility. If this looks good, we'll generate the DocuSign packet and route to procurement.

Best — Mateo
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_privdeploy_term_sheet_v2.pdf; Horizon_MAO_pricing_sheet.xlsx
